inclusion_reason: Livestock mammal with a RefSeq-annotated genome; adds mammal coverage beyond the usual model species; benchmark source to confirm (e.g. Bovine Genome Database).
Bird representative with a well-annotated genome; covers the non-mammalian vertebrate branch; benchmark source to confirm.
Second livestock mammal with RefSeq annotation; useful for testing gene names that differ from human and mouse; benchmark source to confirm.
Amphibian representative; has a dedicated community database (Xenbase) that can act as an answer key.
Insect from a different order than fruit fly; annotated genome; benchmark source to confirm.
Disease-vector insect with an annotated genome; VEuPathDB (VectorBase) is a likely answer key.
Moth representative that widens insect coverage; benchmark source to confirm.
Beetle representative (largest animal order) with an annotated genome; benchmark source to confirm.
Cnidarian outside the bilaterian animals, so it tests distant orthology; benchmark source to confirm.
Major crop monocot with an annotated genome; Gramene or RAP-DB is a likely answer key. NCBI gene data may use the subspecies ID.
Crop monocot with a large genome and many alias names; MaizeGDB is a likely answer key.
Crop eudicot (different plant lineage from rice and maize); Sol Genomics Network is a likely answer key.
Filamentous fungus (not yeast) that adds fungal coverage; FungiDB is a likely answer key. NCBI gene data may use a strain ID.
Parasitic protist with annotated genome; VEuPathDB is a likely answer key. NCBI gene data often uses the 3D7 strain ID.
Amoebozoan protist; dictyBase is a likely answer key. NCBI gene data may use the AX4 strain ID.
"Well-annotated reference genome; useful as the model-species comparison for the non-model species."
